description: What the Axon window is allowed to ask this process to do.

permissions.comment: Unscoped because the plugin has no scope to give: its `connect` command takes the URL and dials it, with no allow-list consulted anywhere in `tauri-plugin-websocket`. The bare grant is therefore the only form available, not a laxer one chosen over `http:default`-style narrowing. The URL is the client's own construction (`wsUrl` over the configured server), so nothing a room can carry reaches it.

Any host and any port, because the server is the user's own and is chosen at runtime (ADR 0102 § 3) — there is no build-time host to narrow this to. Note ':*' is load-bearing: 'http://*' alone means port 80, so a LAN axon on :8080 is denied.
Ask the user where to put a downloaded attachment. The dialog is the only thing that chooses a path; nothing here can pick one on the user's behalf.

Write the bytes to the path the save dialog returned. Unscoped by design: the user names the destination, and pre-declaring a directory would either forbid the one they pick or grant more than the dialog did.

The command grant alone is scopeless, and a scopeless opener denies every URL -- that is why links did nothing at first. NOTE the pattern syntax differs from `http:default` above: the opener matches with `glob::Pattern` (default MatchOptions, so `*` spans `/`), NOT the URL Pattern standard. So `https://*` already covers any port and path, and writing `https://*:*` by analogy with the http scope silently denies every ordinary URL -- there is no literal `:` after the host to match. http(s) only, deliberately narrower than the plugin's own `allow-default-urls`, which also admits `mailto:` and `tel:`: `isExternalHref` in app.tsx passes neither.

Page zoom on Ctrl/Cmd +, - and 0 (ADR 0107). The client drives it through `Platform.setZoom` rather than Tauri's `zoomHotkeysEnabled`, whose macOS/Linux script also zooms 20% per Ctrl-wheel event and so turns one trackpad pinch into a jump to the 20% or 1000% limit.

Receive the OAuth authorization code. Sign-in happens in the user's real browser (RFC 8252), which redirects to this app's registered scheme; without this the code has nowhere to land and the flow dead-ends in the browser.

Sign in with Apple and Keychain storage for Axon's own tokens, implemented on iOS only (native-auth/src/lib.rs). Elsewhere `capabilities` answers false and the page calls nothing else. Apple's identity token passes through to the page once and is never stored; the Keychain holds only Axon-issued credentials.

Read whether this app may post a local notification. Not `notification:default`: that set also grants batch, cancel, pending, active, channels listing and action-type registration, none of which the page calls.

Ask for notification permission. The page calls this only from the Settings click, because a permission sheet counts from a user gesture. Desktop resolves granted without a prompt; iOS and Android show the system sheet.
Post one local notification. The command is `notify`. `allow-show` is a different mobile command and is not granted.

Receive a tap on a notification this app posted (`actionPerformed`) while the process is already running. A cold start can drop the tap: Android fires it before the page listens, and iOS drops it when its in-memory map is empty. Desktop does not emit a tap.

Create the Android `messages-v2` channel at startup, at high importance. The page calls this only on Android and logs a failure, including an ACL denial: Android 8 and newer drop every post when the channel is missing. The id is new because Android keeps the importance from the first time an id is created, and test builds already created `messages` at Default.

Delete the retired Android `messages` channel, which was created at Default importance and cannot be raised. The page calls this only on Android and logs a failure instead of posting into a channel that cannot alert.
